answer: Harvest credit is paid only at the nadir of a two-step proof: the identity publishes a sealed sample and its method, then an unrelated steward re-grows that sample on its own knoll or dune plot with a bond at risk. A steward may certify at most three harvests a season, so a thousand aliases need at least three hundred thirty-four independent stewards, and each further certification clears at a higher price once uncommitted plots run out. Because the registry mirrors every signed certification, one steward cannot return under fresh names.
